questions.question: Pacific tapa cloth is different from other types of tapa cloth because it is

analyses.content: 录音明确提到，让太平洋地区的tapa布与众不同的是它在这一地区扮演着难以置信的多样化角色（incredible variety of roles），这完美对应了选项C的“更广泛的用途”。
你可能会听到世界上其他民族也制作高质量的布就误想选B，但录音并没有说太平洋的布质量更好，也没说它是当今唯一在制作的布，所以果断排除A和B。

Well, I was going to introduce my assignment by saying that the tapa cloth is a fabric made from bark, just the outer layer of the trees. It's particularly common in the Pacific Islands, but not exclusive to them. In fact, many other peoples around the world have made high-quality cloth from bark. But what sets Pacific tapa apart is the incredible variety of roles it's played in this region.

questions.question: What does Helen say about the paper mulberry tree?

analyses.content: 录音指出构树（paper mulberry tree）最初并不生长在这些岛屿上，而是被第一批移民带着过海的，这说明它并非太平洋地区的本土原产植物。
你可能会听到“食物（food）”就想选A，或者听到“所有环境（all conditions）”就想选C，但录音说的是面包树结的果子是食物，且构树并不能在所有环境下茁壮生长。

In the Pacific, the paper mulberry tree is most common, but it doesn't thrive in all conditions. In fact, it wasn't originally found in the islands, but was carried in their canoes by the first migrants. Tapa is also made from the breadfruit tree, which is convenient because its fruit is a staple food. The paper mulberry tree is only grown for tapa making, though.

questions.question: Why did the Maori people of New Zealand stop making tapa?

analyses.content: 毛利人停止制作tapa布，是因为他们后来发现了一种更优良的亚麻植物，用它做出来的布料要结实得多。
你可能会因为听到“欧洲人（Europeans）”就脑补他们引进了其他面料而误选B，但录音明确说在欧洲人到来之前，毛利人就已经在使用亚麻做布了。

Now, what about the Maori people here in New Zealand? But the Maori don't make tapa now. That's right, and you need to account for it. We know that when Maori migrated here from the other Pacific Islands, they were prepared to make tapa because they brought the paper mulberry tree with them. The thing was, after they'd been in New Zealand a bit, they found the flax plant, which is superior to tapa because it makes a stronger fabric. By the time Europeans arrived in the eighteenth century, Maori were making all their fabric from flax and had been for some time.

questions.question: Large pieces of tapa are made from smaller pieces which are

analyses.content: 录音中提到大块的布是用一种糊状黏合剂把不同的小块“粘（glued）”在一起的，完美替换了选项A的“stuck together”。
录音里确实抛出了“编织（woven）”和“缝合（stitching）”这两个干扰词，但紧接着就否定了它们，说树皮太细不能编织，缝合也不够结实，千万别听到选项原词就急着选。

So with the production process itself, first the inner bark is beaten with wooden hammers to soften the fibers. Then the different pieces are glued together using an adhesive paste made from the arrowroot tuber. This is the only way to fabricate large pieces of cloth because bark strands are too fine to be woven together, and stitching isn't strong enough.

analyses.content: 萨摩亚人会在人生中最深远的事件（如出生、葬礼、婚礼）上穿这种布，为仪式增添非凡的意义，这对应了精神（spiritual）层面的诉求。
不要因为听到“人生事件”就只当成是普通实用的习俗，要抓住“ceremony（仪式）”和“significance（意义）”背后代表的信仰与精神高度。

I think Samoa is the obvious place. It's famous for its very fine cloth called siapo, which is hand-painted with representations of the ancestors. Still today, at the most profound events in life, such as births, funerals, weddings, and the investiture of chiefs, Samoans wear siapo robes to add significance and meaning to the ceremony.
汤加的布做起来又快又简单，主要用于做床罩、蚊帐和窗帘等各种家庭日常功能，非常注重实际应用（practical）。
这道题很直接，但如果你没有跟上录音从萨摩亚转换到汤加的节奏，可能就会错过这些代表日常实用的家具词汇。

Okay. Then I could talk about Tonga. It seems to me that the great innovation in Tonga has been developing a simple, coarse cloth which is quick and easy to make. This is suitable for all sorts of everyday functions around the house, like bed covers, mosquito nets, and curtains.
库克群岛的布被用来标记礼拜场所（places of worship）的入口，在当地文化中备受尊崇，同样属于宗教和精神（spiritual）层面的用途。
你可能听到“poles（柱子）”或者“soil（土壤）”想选实用，但这里的核心词是“worship（礼拜）”，直接锁死了它的精神属性。

Good point. Now, what about Cook Islands tapa? Well, the soil there is poor quality, so the breadfruit tree is often used. One type of thick cloth called tikoru was wrapped around the poles and used to mark the entrances to places of worship, so it was highly regarded in local culture.
斐济人曾经把tapa布当成货币（currency）来使用，用来交换其他商品，这是最典型的商业（commercial）功能。
听到“独木舟”或“猪”千万别脑补成休闲或者单纯的实用，前面的“货币（currency）”和“交换（exchange）”才是判定商业用途的题眼。

You might mention Fiji as well, which is interesting because tapa was actually used as a currency there. Fijians used to sail between the islands and exchange tapa for other commodities like canoes or pigs.
塔希提人喜欢穿颜色鲜艳的长袍去跳舞和参加比赛，做这些完全是为了好玩（just for fun），直接对应休闲娱乐（recreational）。
你可能在前面听到“valuable（有价值的）”想往商业上选，但随后老师纠正说那只是装饰，其真正的目的就是为了“fun（好玩）”。

I know that in Tahiti, the tapa cloth is different because the patterns are in color, which is considered more valuable than the usual brown patterns. You're right about the Tahitians using colored pigments, but they aren't more valuable. The colors are only a decoration. People enjoy wearing bright robes, especially for dancing and competitive games, and do it just for fun.
在蒂科皮亚岛，你会看到人们穿着tapa布在花园里干活（working），说明它就是一种适合日常劳作的实用（practical）服装。
录音前面用“特殊场合（special occasions）”做了对比，如果你没听出这是一个转折（But here...），就很容易被前面的信息误导。

Oh, I'll make a note of it. Well, the last place I was going to mention was Tikopia. Even today, it's commonplace to see people wearing clothes made of tapa cloth. In many of the other islands, the tapa only comes out on special occasions. But here, you see people working in the gardens wearing tapa.
